title: Selecting Seed-Bearing Plants
summary: Learn how to observe all your plants throughout their life cycle to choose the best breeders, mark your seed-bearing plants in the field, and move beyond the "biggest vegetable" trap to select vigorous and adapted seeds.

pages.title: Selecting means choosing the future of your garden
pages.text:
When you harvest a seed, you are choosing the children of your garden for next year!
By choosing the best plants, you adapt your crops to your soil, your climate, and your tastes.
This is called **farmer selection**.
It makes your crops stronger and more self-sufficient year after year!
pages.illustration_description: Plan moyen : Une maraîchère souriante et attentive au milieu de ses planches maraîchères en plein soleil. Elle observe avec fierté ses beaux rangs de légumes en excellente santé.

pages.title: The Classic Trap: Only Looking at the Fruit
pages.text:
Many market gardeners make this mistake:
They wait for the harvest and save seeds from the largest vegetable found in the crate.
This is a trap!
A large fruit can come from a fragile plant, one that fell ill right after or was excessively watered.
The seed inherits the entire behavior of the plant, not just the shape of the fruit!
pages.illustration_description:
Comparaison en deux cases :
- À gauche (barrée d'une croix rouge ❌) : Un maraîcher choisit un très gros fruit sur un plant tout jauni et attaqué par des champignons.
- À droite (avec coche verte ✅) : Un maraîcher admire un plant vigoureux, vert foncé, dressé fièrement et portant plusieurs fruits réguliers et sains.

pages.title: First Golden Rule: Observe the Plant from Start to Finish
pages.text:
Good selection begins in the nursery and continues until full maturity!
Observe your plants at each stage of their life:
1. Which seed germinated first with vigor?
2. Which plant withstood the scorching sun well without wilting?
3. Which plant was not attacked by foliage diseases?
pages.illustration_description:
Frise chronologique montrant la vie d'une plante de piment :
- Jeune pousse robuste qui lève droit
- Plant vigoureux en plein soleil de midi sans flétrir
- Plant fleuri et sain
- Plant chargé de piments mûrs avec des feuilles bien vertes.
Flèche continue annotée : "Observer toute la vie du plant ✅".

pages.title: Choosing Your Criteria: Health First
pages.text:
The first absolute criterion is health!
Never save seeds from a **diseased**, **stunted**, or **suspiciously spotted** plant.
Viruses and fungi can reside in the seed and infect your entire next crop.
Choose only **healthy**, **vigorous**, and **upright** plants!
pages.illustration_description:
Gros plan sur deux plants côte à côte :
- L'un présente des feuilles cloquées et tachées de noir (panneau interdit ❌ avec annotation "Maladie — Ne pas récolter les graines !").
- L'autre a un feuillage lustré, bien vert et sain (panneau coché ✅).

pages.title: Choosing Your Criteria: Heat and Drought Resistance
pages.text:
Under the scorching sun and in the dry season:
- Observe your beds during the hottest hours of the day (around 1 PM or 2 PM).
- Some plants completely give up and wilt.
- Others remain upright and keep their leaves firm: these are your champions of resistance!
pages.illustration_description:
Deux plants sous un soleil de plomb ardent (rayons lumineux stylisés) :
- Le premier a les feuilles totalement molles et pendantes vers le sol 👎.
- Le second reste bien dressé, feuilles fermes et dynamiques 👍.

pages.title: Earliness or Extended Harvest: What Do You Want?
pages.text:
Depending on your market or family needs, you can choose what matters most:
- **Earliness**: You identify the first plant that yields ripe vegetables to sell at the best price before everyone else.
- **Productivity**: You choose the plant that produces regularly over a long period.
Make sure to note what you are looking for from the start!
pages.illustration_description:
Deux paniers de récolte :
- L'un annoté "Précoce (premier arrivé au marché avec le meilleur prix 💰)".
- L'autre annoté "Production continue (pour nourrir la famille sur plusieurs mois 🧺)".

pages.title: Taste, Shape, and Firmness: Taste Before You Harvest!
pages.text:
For fruit vegetables (tomatoes, watermelons, cucumbers):
Always taste at least one fruit from the plant you want to keep!
Is it sweet? Does it taste good? Is the skin firm enough to withstand transport?
If a fruit is bitter or mealy, absolutely do not save its seeds, even if the plant is magnificent!
pages.illustration_description:
Le maraîcher coupe une tranche d'une belle tomate directement sur la planche, la goûte les yeux fermés avec un sourire satisfait.
Bulle : "Délicieuse, sucrée et parfumée ! Ce pied donnera de superbes semences ✅".

pages.title: Immediately Mark Selected Plants
pages.text:
As soon as you've identified an exceptional plant, mark it without delay!

- Tie a piece of cloth or a brightly colored ribbon to the main stem.
- Plant a clearly visible stake at its base.

Without marking, you or a worker will instinctively harvest the fruit to eat or sell it!
pages.illustration_description:
Le maraîcher noue un ruban rouge bien visible autour de la tige d'un pied de piment exceptionnel et enfonce un tuteur en bois peint en blanc juste à côté.
Panneau d'avertissement accroché : "Porte-graines — Ne pas cueillir pour la vente ⚠️".

pages.title: Preventing Family and Workers from Harvesting
pages.text:
In a shared plot or with workers:
Clearly explain the meaning of the red ribbon:
"This plant with the red ribbon is our seed stock for next year. Absolutely no harvesting its fruits!"
A ribbon protects months of work from unintentional harvesting.
pages.illustration_description: Le maraîcher montre le plant marqué d'un ruban rouge à deux ouvriers et un membre de sa famille dans le champ. Tout le monde acquiesce d'un signe de tête compréhensif.

pages.title: Making a simple plan in a notebook
pages.text:
Rain, sun, and wind can discolor or dislodge a ribbon.
To be sure not to lose anything:
- Draw the plan of your beds in a simple notebook.
- Note where your seed parents are located (for example: "Bed 3, stake 5: Resistant local tomato").
This plan stays safe at home!
pages.illustration_description:
Plan en plongée sur un carnet ouvert tenu dans une main :
Dessin schématique fait à la main des planches de culture avec des petits repères colorés et le texte manuscrit clair : "Planche Tomates — 3 porte-graines au milieu".

pages.title: Warning: The seed plant lives much longer!
pages.text:
To eat a lettuce or a cucumber, a few weeks are enough.
But to produce living and mature seeds, the plant needs much more time!
A lettuce is eaten after 2 months, but its seeds require 5 to 6 months.
The seed plant will occupy the bed long after the end of ordinary harvests!
pages.illustration_description:
Comparatif de durée avec deux sabliers :
- Laitue pour la salade : 60 jours (feuilles tendres prêtes à couper).
- Laitue porte-graines : 150 jours (haute tige fleurie portant de petits plumets blancs de graines mûres).

pages.title: Group Seed-Bearing Plants in a Dedicated Area
pages.text:
To avoid blocking an entire bed that you need for replanting:
- When possible, reserve a square or an end of your plot to group your seed-bearing plants.
- You will be able to continue watering and monitoring your seeds without disturbing the rest of your market garden!
pages.illustration_description:
Vue d'ensemble d'un potager organisé :
- 4 grandes planches de maraîchage en production courante.
- À l'extrémité, une planche délimitée annotée "Zone des semences — Surveillance et soins spéciaux".

pages.title: Special Case: When NOT to Select?
pages.text:
Sometimes, it is crucial not to perform severe selection:
1. **Rare or endangered variety**: If you only have 5 or 6 plants of an heirloom variety, keep ALL healthy plants to save the variety!
2. **Need for high diversity**: Mixing seeds from different plants creates a "reservoir" capable of withstanding unforeseen events.
Too much culling on a small group weakens the variety.
pages.illustration_description:
Petite poignée de 10 graines rares dans une calebasse.
Schéma montrant que chaque plant germé est précieux et numéroté pour sauver la variété du risque d'extinction.

pages.title: Maintaining a Sufficient Population
pages.text:
To keep your seeds vigorous year after year:
Never harvest seeds from a single plant!
Harvest seeds from several different healthy plants (at least 5 to 10 for tomatoes or peppers, 30 to 50 for corn or cabbage).
Mixing their seeds prevents what is known as **inbreeding** (the depletion of the family).
pages.illustration_description:
Schéma simple :
Plusieurs beaux plants marqués dans la parcelle convergent vers une même calebasse de graines.
Mention : "Mélange des meilleurs plants = variété forte et fertile ✅".

pages.title: The 4 Reflexes of the Market Gardener Breeder
pages.text:
To succeed in your selection each season:
1. **Look at the entire plant**, not just the fruit size.
2. **Prioritize health**, heat tolerance, and taste.
3. **Mark with ribbon** as soon as the champion is spotted.
4. **Harvest from several healthy plants** to maintain the vigor of the variety!
pages.illustration_description: Infographie simple en 4 vignettes avec pictos résumant les 4 étapes fondamentales (Plant entier / Soleil et santé / Ruban rouge / Panier mélangé).

pages.title: Congratulations! You are the creator of your own seeds
pages.text:
Bravo! You now know how to choose your best seeds:
✅ You no longer fall into the trap of the giant fruit on a diseased plant
✅ You know how to spot plants that brave heat and diseases
✅ Your seed parents are marked, protected, and monitored over time

Next module: Isolation techniques to avoid undesirable cross-pollination!
pages.illustration_description:
Le maraîcher sourit fièrement devant sa parcelle, tenant son carnet de terrain à la main, tandis que le vent fait flotter les jolis rubans rouges sur ses plus beaux plants.
Plusieurs coches vertes ✅ et symbole de certification paysanne.
